facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Pararcus is approximately 1.35 meters long and was found in the Lower Muschelkalk formation at Winterswijk.
facts.quote: Pararcus is known from a holotype skeleton about 1.35 m long from the Lower Muschelkalk of Winterswijk.

facts.statement: Pararcus was a marine reptile that lived in the Netherlands during the Middle Triassic period.
facts.quote: Pararcus is an extinct genus of placodont marine reptile from the Middle Triassic of the Netherlands.

facts.statement: Pararcus is classified as a member of the extinct order Placodontia.
facts.quote: Pararcus is an extinct genus of placodont marine reptile

facts.statement: Pararcus belongs to the superorder Sauropterygia and the order Placodontia.
Pararcus lived at the beginning of the Middle Triassic, specifically the Lower Anisian stage.
facts.quote: vivieron a principios del Triásico medio (Anisiense inferior)

facts.statement: Pararcus inhabited the warm waters of what is now the Netherlands in Europe.
facts.quote: Habitaba en las aguas cálidas de lo que es hoy Holanda, Europa.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Pararcus have been found in the Vossenveld formation at Winterswijk.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles han aparecido en la formación Vossenveld, en Winterswijk

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as TWE 480000454, is an incomplete, disarticulated skeleton measuring about 1.35 meters.
facts.quote: el holotipo, TWE 480000454, es un esqueleto incompleto desarticulado, de unos 1,35 metros

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Pararcus is Placodontia.
The genus Pararcus was described by Klein and Scheyer in 2013.
The authority for the genus Pararcus is cited as Klein & Scheyer, 2013.
